costGuide.title: Ferrari F163 Engine Replacement Cost (UK)
costGuide.labourLine: Fitting a Ferrari F163 typically takes 20-30+ hours at £150-£250/hr (specialist Ferrari workshop) due to the complex integration of the MGU-K electric motor, high-voltage cabling, and twin-turbo plumbing .
paragraphs: The primary cost driver for a Ferrari F163 replacement is the hybrid powertrain integration. A quality reconditioned unit must include a fully bench-tested MGU-K motor, updated inverter software, and verified turbocharger assemblies. Attempting to fit an early-production F163 without the latest ECU and battery management calibration will result in immediate hybrid system faults and limp mode. For a detailed breakdown of how these factors affect your final invoice, see our full reconditioned engine cost guide .

failures.title: Ferrari F163 Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: MGU-K / High-Voltage System Faults - 2021-2022 early builds
items.whatHappens: Early software calibration issues or inverter faults can trigger hybrid system shutdowns, limiting the car to combustion-only mode or throwing high-voltage isolation warnings on the dashboard.
items.repairVsReplace: Usually resolved via official Ferrari software updates or inverter replacement under warranty. However, if the MGU-K motor itself has suffered internal electrical failure, a full Ferrari F163 replacement or major hybrid system strip is required.

items.title: Turbocharger Heat Soak and Wastegate Rattle
items.whatHappens: The compact 120-degree V6 layout places the twin turbos inside the V, leading to extreme heat concentration. This can accelerate wastegate actuator wear or cause heat-related degradation of nearby composite intake components.
items.repairVsReplace: Actuator replacement is possible, but severe heat damage to the turbo housing or surrounding intake manifold necessitates a full engine removal and comprehensive rebuild.

failures.goodYearsLine: Post-2023 production runs have received updated hybrid control software and revised thermal management shielding, significantly reducing early teething issues, though the inherent complexity of the system demands strict adherence to official service intervals .

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement Ferrari F163 - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: A used Ferrari F163 is only advisable if it comes with a full Ferrari Classiche or official dealer service history, confirming all hybrid software recalls, battery health checks, and turbocharger inspections have been completed. Given the extreme performance demands, a low-mileage used unit is the absolute bare minimum requirement.

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: A proper reconditioned Ferrari F163 is the recommended choice for most owners. A reputable Ferrari specialist will have bench-tested the MGU-K unit, updated all inverters to the latest calibration, and verified turbocharger integrity. This effectively resets the powertrain's reliability clock while retaining the correct 830 cv hybrid mapping.

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A full rebuild is justified only in cases of severe internal mechanical failure, such as rod bearing wear from extreme track use or oil starvation. This requires a factory-level rebuild environment with specialised tooling to handle the hybrid components safely.

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: Opting for a supply-and-fit service through our network ensures the replacing garage assumes full responsibility for both the unit and the complex high-voltage labour, backed by a minimum 12-month warranty for complete peace of mind.
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: The Ferrari F163 is fitted to the 296 GTB and GTS, which hold exceptionally high retained values (typically £250,000-£350,000+ depending on specification and mileage ). While replacement costs are significant, they represent a small fraction of the vehicle's overall value, making a professional engine replacement the only financially logical choice to preserve the asset.

items.question: How much does a Ferrari F163 engine replacement cost?
items.answer: A reconditioned Ferrari F163 engine typically costs between £25,000 and £40,000 for supply-only, with fully fitted specialist prices ranging from £31,000 to £50,000. Pricing is estimated using Ferrari V8 hybrid benchmarks as a proxy, reflecting the extreme complexity and low-volume nature of the 120-degree V6 hybrid architecture. Labour is highly specialised, typically requiring 20-30+ hours at Ferrari-certified specialist rates to safely manage the high-voltage cabling and MGU-K integration. Used units start around £15,000 but carry immense risk without a verifiable Ferrari Classiche or main dealer service history.

items.question: What is the most common Ferrari F163 engine failure?
items.answer: The most documented issues involve early MGU-K high-voltage system software faults and turbocharger heat soak, typically manifesting in early 2021-2022 production builds. Early software calibration or inverter faults can trigger hybrid system shutdowns, limiting the car to combustion-only mode or throwing high-voltage isolation warnings. The compact 120-degree V6 layout places the twin turbos inside the V, leading to extreme heat concentration that can accelerate wastegate actuator wear or degrade composite intake components. Post-2023 revisions have largely addressed these teething issues via updated thermal shielding and hybrid control software.

items.question: Which Ferrari models use the F163 engine?
items.answer: The Ferrari F163 is a highly exclusive, purpose-built powertrain fitted exclusively to the Ferrari 296 GTB and 296 GTS. It debuted in 2021, marking Ferrari's return to a V6 configuration for its mid-engine sports cars, augmented by a rear-mounted MGU-K electric motor. It is not fitted to the SF90 Stradale (which uses the F154BH V8 hybrid) or the Roma/Portofino (which use the F154CD V8).

items.question: Should I buy a used or reconditioned Ferrari F163 engine?
items.answer: A properly reconditioned Ferrari F163 is strongly recommended over a used unit for this cutting-edge hybrid supercar. A quality reconditioned unit will have the MGU-K motor bench-tested, the inverters updated to the latest factory calibration, and the turbocharger assemblies verified for heat-related wear. Used units are a massive gamble; without documented proof of high-voltage system health and hybrid battery cycles, you risk inheriting catastrophic electrical faults that can ground the vehicle entirely. The cost difference is justified by the comprehensive 12-24 month warranty and the assurance of factory-level hybrid safety protocols.

items.question: How do I confirm my car has the F163 engine code?
items.answer: You can verify the F163 engine code via the vehicle's VIN plate located under the front bonnet, or through an official Ferrari dealer diagnostic scan. The F163 is the exclusive powertrain for the 296 platform, featuring a unique 120-degree V6 block that allows for a lower centre of gravity than the outgoing V8s. Do not confuse it with the F154 family of V8s; the physical dimensions, MGU-K placement, and ECU mapping of the F163 are entirely unique to the 296 chassis.
